newsitem.title: GERMANY: POLL - German sentiment seen rising, M3 growth easing.
newsitem.headline: POLL - German sentiment seen rising, M3 growth easing.

text.p: Any pressure on the Bundesbank to consider raising interest rates will be eased slightly next week with the release of July M3 money supply data, according to a Reuter poll of economists.
At the same time, business sentiment in Germany is expected to pick up, with economists forecasting that the Ifo business sentiment index will show a rise for the fourth month in a row.

M3 growth, which hit the central bank's 3.5 to 6.5 percent target zone for the first time this year in June when it slowed to 6.4 percent from 7.0 percent in May, is seen slowing further in July to 6.3 percent, an average of forecasts shows.
The predictions are for annualised, seasonally-adjusted M3 growth measured against the fourth quarter of 1996.

"The chances are very good that (M3 growth) will remain in the corridor," said Ralf Kugelstadt, economist at UBS in Frankfurt. "The bond and share markets are going well and we should see higher public borrowing levels."
Investment in shares and bonds -- a process called capital formation -- tends to weaken M3 growth rates because it siphons funds out of short-term deposit accounts.
Kugelstadt expects growth in M3, which comprises cash in circulation, time sight and short-term saving deposits, to slow to 6.2 percent in July.

While a pronounced decline in the mark versus the dollar, threatening to filter through to inflationary pressure, has prompted talk of a possible Bundesbank rate hike in the coming months, analysts said July's M3 data should take some of the sting out of that speculation.

Germany's export sector has been one of the main beneficiaries of the falling mark, since it makes German goods less expensive abroad. Analysts said this would continue to have a positive effect on business sentiment.

"In the light of the higher dollar and higher capacity utilisation in the second quarter of the year, the Ifo index should rise again this time," said Lothar Hessler at Trinkaus Capital Management in Duesseldorf.
The Ifo index is expected to rise to 96.6 in July from 96.00, average forecasts show.
"There won't be a major breakthrough in the Ifo index," said Eckhard Schulte, economist at IBJ in Frankfurt. "But business expectations have certainly improved."

Looking further ahead, analysts said Germany's economic recovery was likely to continue to boost business sentiment, but was also likely to prevent money supply growth from slowing much further, economists said.

Most of those surveyed expected M3 growth to remain near the upper boundary of the Bundesbank's 3.5 to 6.5 percent zone, but Michael Schubert economist at Commerzbank in Frankfurt said there was a risk it could break out again later in the year.

"We're sceptical about whether money supply growth will remain in the corridor," he said. "With a moderate economic recovery, money supply could also grow moderately. It will certainly be difficult to reach the bottom half of the corridor."
